title: Committee of Supply – Head N (Ministry of Foreign Affairs)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head N (Ministry of Foreign Affairs)

sections.label: Budget cut for Head N
sections.summary: A motion is made to reduce Head N of the Estimates by $100, recalling last year's COS description of US-China ties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Chairman, I seek to move, "That the sum to be allocated for Head N of the Estimates be reduced by $100".

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In the Committee of Supply (COS) last year, the United States (US)-China relationship was described as the "most consequential" for international affairs.

sections.label: US tariffs on neighbours
sections.summary: After the last US election, the new administration's first month included plans to impose tariffs on Canada and Mexico under NAFTA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Following the last election in the US, the new administration in its first month in office included plans to impose tariffs on Canada and Mexico, the US' closest neighbours and important trading partners under the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA).

sections.label: US vote at UN
sections.summary: The US voted with Russia and North Korea against a UN resolution by Western allies condemning the invasion of Ukraine.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The most obvious evidence of this rift was US voting along with Russia and North Korea against a resolution in the United Nations (UN) put forward by its Western allies condemning the invasion of Ukraine.

sections.label: US investment in Singapore
sections.summary: The US is Singapore's largest foreign investor, with over US$600 billion invested in Singapore in 2023.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Economically, the US is also our largest foreign investor, with over US$600 billion invested in Singapore in 2023.

sections.label: Trade rules and tariffs
sections.summary: Singapore thrives on integrity of global trade routes and rules-based norms, and unilateral tariffs or sanctions can batter its economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Singapore thrives because of the integrity of global trade routes and rules-based norms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Any unilateral tariff or sanction, imposed on a whim by the major powers, can batter our economy.

sections.label: Principles over sides
sections.summary: Singapore picks no sides but picks principles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Simply put, we pick no sides; we pick principles.

sections.label: United ASEAN against big powers
sections.summary: A united ASEAN is described as the best bet against big power rivalries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: A united ASEAN is our best bet against the crosswinds of big power rivalries.

sections.label: Diversifying Singapore's economic ties
sections.summary: Singapore should diversify its economy by strengthening trade and investment ties with ASEAN, the EU, India, Japan, South Korea and other growing economies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To mitigate these risks, Singapore should diversify its economy by strengthening trade investment ties with ASEAN and the EU, as well as with India, Japan, South Korea and other growing economies, ensuring that these relationships are based on stable and predictable legal and institutional frameworks.

sections.label: US withdrawal from WHO, Paris
sections.summary: The US has announced it will withdraw from the World Health Organisation and the Paris Climate Agreement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: More troublingly, the US has also announced it will withdraw from the World Health Organisation and the Paris Climate Agreement.

sections.label: Pact of the Future adoption
sections.summary: World leaders adopted the Pact of the Future at the UN Summit of the Future in September last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: In September last year, at the Summit of the Future, under the auspices of the UN, world leaders adopted the Pact of the Future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: This aims to reinvigorate and better position multilateral institutions to address complex challenges at a time when multilateralism itself is under pressure.

sections.label: US-China rivalry and foreign policy
sections.summary: A third part marked by economic decoupling and US-China rivalry raises how Singapore's foreign policy can be future-proofed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: And the third part, which emerged from the mid-2010s, has been marked by increasing economic decoupling and geopolitical tensions, with global affairs shaped largely through the lens of US-China rivalry.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Now, with the incoming Trump Administration triggering off tectonic shifts in both global trade and geopolitics, we could be entering a disorderly interregnum.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: As we celebrate SG60, how can we ensure that Singapore's foreign policy is sufficiently future-proofed for the challenges ahead?

sections.label: US-Singapore trade and defence ties
sections.summary: The passage states US-Singapore trade, investment and defence agreements, including training detachments in Idaho, Arizona and Texas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: On the trade front, the US-Singapore Free Trade Agreement was signed in 2004.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: According to data from MFA, we have over 5,800 US companies based in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: Our bilateral trade and Singapore's investments in the US in more than 30 states have supported over a quarter million jobs for Americans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: In relation to defence, we have signed several important defence agreements with the US and have training detachments in Idaho, Arizona and Texas, which make us the second largest permanent foreign military contingent in the US.

sections.label: US concerns on Nvidia chips
sections.summary: The US expressed concerns that Nvidia chips may have moved through Singapore to China, breaching US trade restrictions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: Recently, the US expressed concerns that some US technologies, specifically, Nvidia chips, may have been moved through Singapore to China, in breach of US trade restrictions on such chips.

sections.label: Singapore trade dependence
sections.summary: The US is a large trading partner, and Singapore's economy depends on trade, so global trade disruption can affect its growth and stability.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The US is one of Singapore's largest trading partners.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Singapore's economy is highly dependent on trade and any disruption to global trade can have significant impact on Singapore's economic growth and stability.

sections.label: Singapore investment in China
sections.summary: Singapore invested early in China's urbanisation, with projects like Suzhou Industrial Park and Tianjin Eco-City, and expanded financial collaboration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
sentences.text: Singapore was an early investor in China's rapid urbanisation, with landmark projects like the Suzhou Industrial Park project and later, the Tianjin Eco-City project.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
sentences.text: Financial collaboration is also expanded, with Singapore becoming a key offshore hub for RMB internationalisation and Singapore being the host of Chinese companies as a gateway for Southeast Asian expansion.

sections.label: MFA engagement and China ties
sections.summary: MFA is adapting public engagement on foreign policy, and this year marks 35 years of Singapore-China diplomatic ties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: How is MFA adapting its public engagement strategies to make foreign policies more accessible and relevant to Singaporeans and ensure unity in approach?

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: This year marks 35 years of diplomatic ties between Singapore and China, a relationship built on mutual trust, respect for international norms and adherence to global principles.

sections.label: Malaysia-Singapore Leaders' Retreat agreements
sections.summary: At the 11th Malaysia-Singapore Leaders' Retreat in January 2025, agreements were signed, including an MOU and the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
sentences.text: At the 11th Malaysia-Singapore Leaders' Retreat co-chaired by Prime Minister Lawrence Wong and Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim in January 2025, a host of agreements was signed, including an MOU on higher education and an exchange of letters on the Malaysia-Singapore English Volunteers Programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
sentences.text: Both prime ministers also witnessed the exchange of an agreement on the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone, which will harness the complementary strengths of Singapore and Johor to attract new investment projects globally.

sections.label: Singapore-Indonesia landmark agreements
sections.summary: In 2024, three landmark agreements were signed with Indonesia covering airspace, extradition and military training.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: In 2024, three landmark agreements were signed with Indonesia covering areas, such as airspace, extradition and military training.

sections.label: Singapore-Indonesia cooperation discussions
sections.summary: During PM Wong's November 2024 visit, both sides discussed deepening cooperation in defence, trade, digital technologies and healthcare, plus Indonesia's priority sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: During Prime Minister Wong's last visit in November 2024, both sides discussed deepening cooperation in defence, trade and investments, digital technologies and healthcare in addition to Indonesia's priority sectors, such as food security, energy security and human capital development.

sections.label: Currency agreement and defence ties
sections.summary: The Currency Interchangeability Agreement since 1967, defence collaborations and people-to-people ties make the relationship a model of trust and partnership.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: From the Currency Interchangeability Agreement, which has linked our economies since 1967, to regular defense collaborations and warm people-to-people ties, our relationship is a model of trust and partnership.

sections.label: ASEAN growth and pressing challenges
sections.summary: ASEAN's economy grew an estimated 4.5% in 2024, but pressing challenges demand immediate attention.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong
sentences.text: Chairman, while ASEAN's economy grew by an estimated 4.5% in 2024, we are confronted with pressing challenges that demand immediate attention.

sections.label: Red Sea crisis and SME digitalisation
sections.summary: The Red Sea shipping crisis raised freight costs up to five times, and a 2023 survey found three in four ASEAN-5 SMEs in early digitalisation stages.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong
sentences.text: The recent Red Sea shipping crisis, which caused freight costs to surge by up to five times, has severely impacted our export dependent economies.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong
sentences.text: Third, despite ASEAN's commitment to digital transformation, a 2023 survey of 750 SMEs across ASEAN-5 found that three in four SMEs remain in the early stages of digitalisation.

sections.label: Myanmar conflict food insecurity displacement
sections.summary: The United Nations for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs estimates 15 million face acute food insecurity and 3.5 million are internally displaced by the conflict.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The United Nations for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs estimates that 15 million people face acute food insecurity and 3.5 million people are internally displaced due to the conflict.

sections.label: Five-Point Consensus slow implementation
sections.summary: ASEAN's Five-Point Consensus has been criticised for slow implementation, worsened by Myanmar's complex situation and deep distrust between warring parties.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: ASEAN's Five-Point Consensus has been criticised for its slow implementation, which is not helped by the complex situation in Myanmar and the deep distrust between the warring parties.

sections.label: Global shift from unipolarity
sections.summary: The world is shifting from unipolarity, free trade, multilateralism, globalisation, openness and optimism to multipolarity, protectionism, unilateralism, hyper-nationalism, xenophobia and anxiety.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Unfortunately, the world is now shifting from unipolarity to multipolarity, from free trade to protectionism, from multilateralism to unilateralism, from globalisation to hyper-nationalism, from openness to xenophobia, from optimism to anxiety.

sections.label: New world order characteristics
sections.summary: A new world order is taking shape and is characterised by profound unpredictability, instability and volatility.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: A new world order is taking shape and is characterised by profound unpredictability, instability and volatility.

sections.label: US share of global GDP
sections.summary: Post-World War II the US held 40% of global GDP, which has declined to around 26% today though its nominal GDP has grown tremendously.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Post-World War II, the US had a disproportionate share of global gross domestic product (GDP) at 40%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Today, the US’ share of global GDP has declined to around 26%, although in absolute nomimal terms, its GDP has grown tremendously.

sections.label: Singapore not directly targeted
sections.summary: Singapore, so far, has not been targeted directly.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Singapore, so far, has not been targeted directly.

sections.label: Open paradigm at risk
sections.summary: The open paradigm that Singapore survived and thrived under for six decades is now at risk.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: And that is how we have survived and thrived for six decades.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: This open paradigm that has served us so well for six decades is now at risk.

sections.label: US AI rule and China retaliation
sections.summary: The US AI Diffusion Rule will limit export of advanced AI chips, and China's retaliatory restrictions on critical minerals will disrupt supply chains and raise production costs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: For instance, the US’ AI Diffusion Rule, although not yet finalised and is still subject to changes, but this rule essentially will limit the export of advanced chips that are essential for AI.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: China’s retaliatory restrictions on its own export of critical minerals to the US will also disrupt supply chains, raise production costs and have an impact on global research and development and innovation.

sections.label: Nuclear states and Ukraine
sections.summary: After Ukraine, no nuclear or proto-nuclear state is likely to give up its nuclear option, making the world more dangerous.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: After what has happened to Ukraine, I doubt any current nuclear or proto-nuclear weapon state will ever give up its nuclear option, and all this makes for a much more dangerous world.

sections.label: Rules-based order at risk
sections.summary: The rules-based international order of 80 years risks degenerating into the law of the jungle, where might makes right.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: The rules-based international order that has prevailed for 80 years at risk of degenerating into the law of the jungle, where “might makes right”.

sections.label: Singapore's three core strengths
sections.summary: Singapore's core strengths rest on economic strength and reserves, self-defence, and domestic cohesion.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Our core strengths are based on three key pillars: first, our economic strength and our reserves; second, our ability to stand on our two feet and to defend ourselves; and third, our domestic cohesion.

sections.label: Hamas attack as terror
sections.summary: The attack by Hamas on 7 October 2023 was an act of terror.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: The attack by Hamas on 7 October 2023 was an act of terror.

sections.label: Israel, Gaza and two-state solution
sections.summary: Self-defence must follow international law, Israel's response has gone too far, and Singapore supports a negotiated two-state solution and aid to Gaza.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: At the same time, that right of self-defence must be consistent with international law, humanitarian law and the Geneva conventions, and that is why we told Israel, directly and personally, that Israel's military response has gone too far.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Singapore's long-standing position on the Israeli-Palestinian issue is that the only path to a just, durable and comprehensive peace is a negotiated two-state solution, and we have consistently supported the right of the Palestinian people to a homeland of their own since the 1960s.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: To this end, we will continue to support the Palestinian Authority to build the capacity and to prepare for eventual statehood, and we do so through our enhanced technical assistance package.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: But that is not enough, because we all do feel deep sympathy for the immense suffering of the civilians, and thus far, Singapore and Singaporeans have contributed seven tranches of aid and monetary donations to Gaza worth over $19 million – and we will do more.

sections.label: Ties with US and China
sections.summary: Singapore should maintain ties with both the US and China given its significant equities with both.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: So, Mr Mark Lee, Mr Henry Kwek, Mr Vikram Nair, Ms Poh Li San have asked how we can continue to build on our honest and constructive relations with the US and China, amidst their rivalry.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: I believe it is crucial that we maintain our ties with both countries, given our significant equities with both.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: The US is the largest foreign investor in Singapore, by far.

sections.label: China top goods trading partner
sections.summary: China is Singapore's top trading partner in goods.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Meanwhile, China is our top trading partner in goods.

sections.label: Indonesia framework agreements in force
sections.summary: Expanded framework agreements with Indonesia on airspace, defence and extradition entered into force last year, and Prime Minister Lawrence Wong was the first foreign leader to visit Jakarta after President Prabowo took office.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: With Indonesia, the expanded framework agreements on airspace, defence and extradition entered into force last year, and this was a major achievement.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: In fact, Prime Minister Lawrence Wong was the first foreign leader to visit Jakarta after President Prabowo took office.

sections.label: ASEAN economic integration efforts
sections.summary: Singapore seeks to deepen ASEAN economic integration, aiming to conclude the ATIGA Upgrade and DEFA this year, and notes its network of 27 FTAs covering 90% of trade.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We must also do far more with one another and double down on ASEAN's economic integration in order to improve our collective value proposition and collective resilience, especially in food and energy.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We are looking to conclude negotiations on the ASEAN Trade in Goods Agreement Upgrade this year, which will grow intra-ASEAN trade.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We are also making progress in new economic areas.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We aim to conclude the Digital Economy Framework Agreement (DEFA) this year and we are making progress on the ASEAN Power Grid.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: I can say my diplomats have worked very hard to expand our network of overlapping circles of friends.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We already have an extensive network of 27 free trade agreements (FTAs) that cover 90% of our trade.

sections.label: ROK joins digital agreement
sections.summary: The Republic of Korea became the latest entrant to this agreement in 2024, with other aspirants in discussion, and EU-Singapore Digital Trade Agreement negotiations concluded in July 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: The Republic of Korea (ROK) became the latest entrant to this agreement in 2024 and there are several other aspirants in the queue with whom we are in discussion.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We have also concluded negotiations on the EU-Singapore Digital Trade Agreement in July 2024.

sections.label: Reform over revolution, Pact of Future
sections.summary: Singapore's mantra favours reform over revolution, and it welcomed the adoption of the Pact of the Future, Global Digital Compact and Declaration on Future Generations at the 2024 Summit for the Future.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Our mantra is that it is better to reform than to risk a revolution that will destroy the old regime, the old order, the old arrangements completely, because the alternative is bad for small states.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: That is why we welcomed the adoption of the Pact of the Future, the Global Digital Compact and the Declaration on Future Generations at the Summit for the Future in 2024.

sections.label: UNCLOS navigation and overflight framework
sections.summary: UNCLOS provides the legal framework ensuring freedom of navigation and overflight is a right, not exercised only by the grace of any resident big power.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: The United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) provides the legal framework that ensures that freedom of navigation and overflight is a right and not exercised only by the grace of any resident big power.

sections.label: Nomination and openness and trust
sections.summary: She brought all parties together to arrive at the treaty by consensus, and is being nominated for the International Court of Justice elections due in November 2026; maintaining access to frontier technology requires openness and trust.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Again, she very skillfully managed to bring all parties together, arrive at the treaty, by consensus.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We are nominating her for the International Court of Justice elections due in November 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: The short answer to the question Members have raised on how to maintain our access to frontier technology, the short answer is: openness and trust.

sections.label: Dangerous phase of world order
sections.summary: The most dangerous phase is when one world order is being replaced by a new world order.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: The most dangerous phase is when one world order is being replaced by a new world order.

sections.label: Unity amid tumult and volatility
sections.summary: Singapore must stay principled, calm, confident, relevant, useful and an honest broker, and needs the support and unity of all Singaporeans to face the future with confidence and emerge stronger.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We must stay principled, calm, confident and continue to be relevant, useful, to be an honest broker.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We need the support and unity of all Singaporeans – all of the Members inside this House and Singaporeans outside the Parliament – to forge an unbreakable unity in the midst of great tumult and volatility.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: And if we can do so, then we can face the future with confidence and Singapore will emerge stronger.

sections.label: Change in US policy
sections.summary: After Russia's invasion of Ukraine, Europeans and Americans defended Ukraine and isolated Russia, but the US joining Russia in voting against a UN resolution on 24 February and a live video argument between the US and Ukraine Presidents on 28 February underlined a fundamental change in US policy and cast doubts over its commitment to NATO allies.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Since Russia's invasion of Ukraine, the Europeans and Americans responded forcefully to defend Ukraine and isolate Russia.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: But the US joining Russia in voting against a UN resolution sponsored by Europe and Ukraine on 24 February, identifying Russia as the aggressor, as well as the recent live video showing the argument between the US and Ukraine Presidents on 28 February has dramatically underlined a fundamental change in US policy and cast doubts over its commitment to its NATO allies.

sections.label: Singapore affected by increased tariffs
sections.summary: Singapore has not been targeted directly for now but will be affected, as increased tariffs reshape global supply chains and impact world trade, affecting Singapore as an international port dependent on transhipments.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Singapore has not been targeted directly for now but will certainly be affected.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Increased tariffs will reshape global supply chains and impact the volume and patterns of world trade.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: This will certainly affect Singapore, as an international port heavily dependent on transhipments.

sections.label: Fraying trust in trading system
sections.summary: The consensus and trust underpinning the rules-based international trading system is now fraying.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: The consensus and trust underpinning the rules-based international trading system is now fraying.

sections.label: Singapore calls for Ukraine peace
sections.summary: Singapore has consistently called for an expeditious end to the Russia-Ukraine war and for comprehensive, just, lasting peace under international law and the UN Charter.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Singapore has consistently called for an expeditious end to the war between Russia and Ukraine and for both sides to find comprehensive, just, and lasting peace in accordance with international law and the United Nations Charter.

sections.label: National Service and defence spending
sections.summary: Since independence, Singapore has had National Service and consistently spent between 3% and 6% of GDP on defence.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Ever since independence, we have had National Service and consistently spent between 3% to 6% of GDP on defence.

sections.label: Opposition questions budget surpluses
sections.summary: Some Opposition Members questioned the Government's budgeting approach, suggesting Budget surpluses equate to excessive taxation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: A few days ago, some Opposition Members were questioning the Government's budgeting approach in this House, suggesting that the presence of Budget surpluses equates excessive taxation.

sections.label: Small state becomes trusted hub
sections.summary: Despite small size and lack of natural resources, Singapore became a trusted partner and regional hub through its business environment and rule of law.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Despite our small size and lack of natural resources, we have developed into a trusted partner and regional hub by virtue of our good business environment and sound rule of law.

sections.label: Social cohesion and global partnerships
sections.summary: Singapore must prevent social fragmentation, leverage its trusted reputation, and work with like-minded countries and major powers including the US, China, Europe and India.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: We must be vigilant to prevent social fragmentation or polarisation and ensure that social cohesion is not compromised.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: We can and should continue to leverage our good reputation as a consistent, reliable and trusted partner, to strengthen our links with more countries, and work with like-minded countries bilaterally and multilaterally to uphold and shape global rules and frameworks.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Following many years of tending the garden, Singapore enjoys frequent interactions and benefits from substantive collaboration with major powers and major economies, including the US, China, Europe and India.

sections.label: World confronting technological revolution
sections.summary: The world is confronting a technological revolution on several fronts: AI and digital technologies, biotechnology and sustainable energy.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: The first thing is that the world is confronting a technological revolution on several fronts: AI and digital technologies, biotechnology and sustainable energy.

sections.label: Frontier technologies opportunity and openness
sections.summary: Frontier technologies are an area of great opportunity, but seizing them requires remaining open to people, ideas, technology and business models.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: And the frontier technologies are actually an area of great opportunity for us.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Then, I also took pains to explain, however, that if we are going to seize these opportunities, we must remain open – open to people, ideas, technology, business models.

sections.label: Balancing act, tariffs and export controls
sections.summary: Singapore has maintained a careful balancing act requiring credibility and unity, amid tariffs and unilateral export controls it is not obliged to enforce.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: I would say from experience, so far, we have been able to maintain this very careful balancing act, and it calls for credibility and it calls for unity.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: I explained in Parliament, I think was two weeks ago, that not only are tariffs being applied but export controls are being applied, unilateral export controls that we are not obliged to enforce.

sections.label: Singapore as team-building location
sections.summary: Singapore is described as the most amenable, safe and conducive place to create an effective multinational team taking frontier technologies to world markets.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Maybe it is a dream, but the best place in the world where you can create a team of Russians and Ukrainians and Chinese and South Americans and Africans and Singaporeans – an effective team to take frontier technologies to the markets across the world – the most amenable, safe, conducive place should be Singapore.

sections.label: EU, ASEAN and multilateralism
sections.summary: The EU has been enthusiastic about multilateralism and international law, and the EU, ASEAN and possibly parts of Africa and South America can still sign Free Trade Agreements.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: One regional grouping who has been quite enthusiastic to keep the system of multilateralism and international law going is the EU.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: And that is why I have said to the extent that the EU and ASEAN, and maybe parts of Africa and South America, are still capable of signing Free Trade Agreements, still binding ourselves to international law, because we still believe that in the long run this provides for peace, prosperity and the peaceful resolution of disputes.

sections.label: Singapore humanitarian aid to Gaza
sections.summary: Since October 2023, Singaporeans have delivered seven tranches of humanitarian aid to Gaza totalling over $19 million, with a fundraiser raising $166,000 in one week.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
sentences.text: Since October 2023, Singaporeans have come together to deliver seven tranches of humanitarian aid to Gaza, totalling over $19 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
sentences.text: Just two days ago, the M³@Towns Aid for Gaza fundraiser, through collaboration with the Rahmatan Lil Alamin Foundation (RLAF), raised $166,000 in just one week, and will continue to do so till 6 April.

sections.label: Gaza aid and regional contributions
sections.summary: Seven tranches totalling over $19 million in humanitarian assistance were delivered to Gaza, while Malaysia contributed RM45 million and Indonesia doubled its UNRWA contribution.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: In total, seven tranches totalling over $19 million worth of humanitarian assistance had been delivered to Gaza.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: Since October 2023, Malaysia, for instance, has contributed RM45 million as of November 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: Indonesia last year doubled its annual contribution to UNRWA to US$1.2 million.

sections.label: Singapore-India trade and strategic partnership
sections.summary: Singapore is India's second largest investor and India is Singapore's 12th largest trade partner, with ties elevated to a comprehensive strategic partnership in September last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
sentences.text: Singapore is the second largest investor in India and India is Singapore's 12th largest trade partner.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
sentences.text: As a small trading nation, it makes sense for Singapore to maintain friendly relations with all the major powers in the world like the US, China, Russia and India.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
sentences.text: I understand that in September last year, during the visit of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the relationship between Singapore and India was elevated to a comprehensive strategic partnership.

sections.label: Singapore-Gulf Cooperation Council FTA
sections.summary: Singapore was the first country outside the Middle East to conclude an FTA with the Gulf Cooperation Council, which entered into force on 1 September 2013.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Singapore was the first country outside of the Middle East to conclude an FTA with the Gulf Cooperation Council which entered into force on 1 September 2013.

sections.label: Singapore entities in Cairo
sections.summary: In 2023, the Port of Singapore Authority inaugurated its new head office in Cairo and Changi Airport International studied establishing the Cairo Cargo City.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In 2023, the Port of Singapore Authority inaugurated their new head office in Cairo and Changi Airport International conducted a feasibility study to establish the Cairo Cargo City.

sections.label: Pacific Alliance-Singapore FTA progress
sections.summary: The question asks the Minister to share a progress report on how the Pacific Alliance-Singapore Free Trade Agreement with Chile, Colombia, Peru and Mexico has benefited relationships and trade.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Would the Minister share with the House a progress report of how the Pacific Alliance-Singapore Free Trade Agreement (PASFTA) with Chile, Colombia, Peru and Mexico has benefited our relationships and trade?

sections.label: Digital trade, anniversaries, ICJ nomination
sections.summary: Singapore concluded EU-Singapore Digital Trade Agreement negotiations last year, will mark 50 years with ROK and 60 with Japan, and will nominate Ambassador Rena Lee for the ICJ in November 2026.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
sentences.text: More recently, we concluded negotiations with the EU on the EU-Singapore Digital Trade Agreement (EUSDTA) last year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: We have, as Minister Balakrishnan described earlier, deep engagements with ASEAN, China and India, but there are other important and long-standing relationships in the region.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: We will celebrate milestone diplomatic anniversaries with the Republic of Korea (ROK) and Japan: 50 years with ROK this year and 60 years with Japan next year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, the Government will nominate Ambassador Rena Lee as a candidate for the Judge of the International Court of Justice (ICJ) at the elections in November 2026.

sections.label: Daren Tang WIPO appointment
sections.summary: Mr Daren Tang's 2020 appointment as Director-General of the Geneva-based World Intellectual Property Organisation brought pride to Singapore and recognition of his credentials and Singapore's intellectual property reputation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
sentences.text: When Mr Daren Tang was appointed as the Director-General of the Geneva-based World Intellectual Property Organisation (WIPO) in 2020, it brought pride to Singapore and it is not only a recognition by the international IP community of Mr Tang's credentials, but also of Singapore's reputation as a jurisdiction in being among the best in intellectual protections.

sections.label: Singapore Cooperation Programme established 1992
sections.summary: The Singapore Cooperation Programme was established in 1992 to pay forward help Singapore received in its formative years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: In 1992, the Singapore Cooperation Programme (SCP) was established in our effort to pay forward the help we received in our formative years.

sections.label: Singaporeans travel new destinations, overseas missions
sections.summary: Singaporeans increasingly travel to less-travelled destinations, and over 50 overseas missions serve as contact points for Singaporeans in distress abroad.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
sentences.text: Singaporeans are no longer sticking to the usual destinations but, increasingly, also to less-travelled destinations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
sentences.text: We have over 50 overseas missions worldwide, and these missions serve as a critical point of contact for Singaporeans in distress abroad.

sections.label: Consular support without diplomatic mission
sections.summary: The passage asks how MFA ensures Singaporeans in countries without an on-ground diplomatic mission can access prompt consular support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
sentences.text: Other than contacting the 24-hour MFA Duty Office hotline in times of need, could the MFA share how it ensures that Singaporeans in need, even in countries without an on-ground diplomatic mission, can still access prompt and effective consular support?

sections.label: MFA consular efforts and technology 2024
sections.summary: The passage asks about key highlights of MFA's consular efforts in 2024 and efforts to leverage technology for consular services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
sentences.text: What are some of the key highlights of MFA's consular efforts in 2024?

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
sentences.text: And could MFA share its efforts to leverage technology to improve the delivery of consular services for Singaporeans?

sections.label: MFA digital platforms foreign policy engagement
sections.summary: The passage asks how MFA harnesses digital platforms to engage Singaporeans on foreign policy issues as social media shapes public perception.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong
sentences.text: With social media playing an even larger role in shaping public perception, how is MFA harnessing digital platforms to engage Singaporeans on foreign policy issues?

sections.label: Hostages held by Hamas, ceasefire agreement
sections.summary: The passage states concern about hostages held captive by Hamas for over 500 days and welcomes the multi-phase ceasefire agreement reached recently.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: At the same time, we remain deeply concerned about the hostages still held captive by Hamas for over 500 days now.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: We take some comfort and welcome the multi-phase ceasefire agreement reached recently.

sections.label: Negotiated two-state solution
sections.summary: Singapore states the only viable path to a comprehensive, just and durable solution is a negotiated two-state solution consistent with UN Security Council resolutions.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: First, we believe that the only viable path to a comprehensive, just, and durable solution to this conflict, is a negotiated two-state solution, consistent with the relevant UN Security Council resolutions.

sections.label: Palestine UN membership vote
sections.summary: Singapore voted in favour of a May 2024 UN General Assembly resolution supporting Palestine's admission as a UN member and is prepared in-principle to recognise Palestinian statehood.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: In May 2024, we voted in favour of a resolution at the UN General Assembly supporting the admission of Palestine as a UN member.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Singapore is prepared in-principle to recognise Palestinian statehood and will make this move at the appropriate time.

sections.label: Israel and Jerusalem measures
sections.summary: Singapore has called upon Israel to rescind all unilateral measures taken to change the status of Jerusalem.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Third, Singapore has called upon Israel to rescind all unilateral measures taken to change the status of Jerusalem.

sections.label: Condemning Hamas terror acts
sections.summary: Singapore has consistently condemned acts of terror committed by groups such as Hamas.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: (In Malay):   Chairman, this table shows our consistent position and votes supporting the relevant resolutions on the Palestinian issue   Fourth, Singapore has consistently condemned acts of terror committed by groups such as Hamas.

sections.label: No working with Hamas
sections.summary: Singapore cannot and will not work with any group, including Hamas, that refuses to renounce terrorism and rejects Israel's right to exist.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: Singapore cannot and will not work with any group, including Hamas, which refuses to renounce terrorism, and in fact, continue to use terrorism to achieve their aims and rejects the right of Israel to exist.

sections.label: Self-defence and Gaza response
sections.summary: Singapore says it would assert its right to self-defence under Article 51 of the UN Charter, but has made clear Israel's military response in Gaza has gone too far.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: In a scenario where Singapore is subject to an armed attack, we would similarly need to assert and exercise our right to self-defence as provided under Article 51 of the UN Charter.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: However, we have made clear, including in our interactions with the Israelis, that their military response in Gaza has gone too far.

sections.label: Calls to sever Israel ties
sections.summary: Some have asked why Singapore does not sever all ties with Israel and impose unilateral sanctions in support of Palestine.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: Some have asked why Singapore does not sever all ties with Israel.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: They want Singapore to impose unilateral sanctions on it, in support of Palestine.

sections.label: Relations with Israel benefits
sections.summary: Continued relations with Israel let Singapore convey candid views to Israeli leaders and facilitated RSAF aid clearances and food transport via Ashdod port.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: Our continued relations with Israel allow us to directly convey our candid views on the conflict to Israeli leaders, including our view that their actions have crossed the line.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: It has also facilitated the RSAF’s efforts to obtain the necessary clearances from Israel to convey humanitarian aid via airdrops last year, as well as to convey food items into Gaza which were transported via the Ashdod port in Israel.

sections.label: Humanitarian assistance to Gaza
sections.summary: Singapore has provided seven tranches of humanitarian assistance to Gaza totalling $19 million over the past 16 months.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: This is a strong reflection of our identity and shared values as a compassionate, inclusive, and cohesive society.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: We have provided seven tranches of humanitarian assistance to Gaza with $19 million over the past 16 months.

sections.label: SG60 M3 fundraising project
sections.summary: An SG60 project by M3, targeting $600,000 for Singapore's 60th year of independence, raised $166,000 in its first week.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: With a target of raising $600,000 as we commemorate our 60th year of independence, this SG60 project by M3 has raised $166,000 in its first week alone.

sections.label: Singapore-Saudi Strategic Partnership Council
sections.summary: Singapore will establish a Strategic Partnership Council co-chaired by Prime Minister Lawrence Wong and Saudi Crown Prince Prince Mohammed Bin Salman.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: Singapore will establish a Strategic Partnership Council, to be co-chaired by Prime Minister Lawrence Wong and Saudi Crown Prince and Prime Minister His Royal Highness Prince Mohammed Bin Salman.

sections.label: Singapore-UAE Comprehensive Partnership cooperation
sections.summary: Under the Singapore-UAE Comprehensive Partnership signed in 2019, the two continue deepening cooperation in public service, AI and civil nuclear energy.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: Under the Singapore-UAE Comprehensive Partnership signed in 2019, we continue to deepen our multifaceted cooperation in fields, such as public service cooperation, AI and civil nuclear energy.

sections.label: Qatar and Oman Engagements
sections.summary: Qatar will host the third Implementing Monitoring Mechanism, and Singapore co-chaired the second Singapore-Oman Strategic Dialogue in Muscat in January 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: Qatar will host the third Implementing Monitoring Mechanism later this year, which will facilitate further bilateral partnerships and initiatives.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: Minister Shanmugam and I co-chaired the second Singapore-Oman Strategic Dialogue in Muscat in January 2025, where we discussed ways to strengthen collaboration in digital economy, renewable energy and security cooperation.

sections.label: Latin America Trade Agreements
sections.summary: Visits to Latin America explored broadening ties using Singapore's free trade agreements with MERCOSUR and the Pacific Alliance.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: During my visits last year to Latin America, I explored ways to broaden our political and economic ties, by leveraging free trade agreements that Singapore had signed with the Southern Common Market (MERCOSUR) and the Pacific Alliance.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: These agreements, when entered into force, will increase opportunities for trade and investment, lower the costs of trade for our companies, create jobs for Singaporeans and grow our economy.

sections.label: Africa Engagement and G20
sections.summary: Singapore will host the Singapore-Africa Ministerial Exchange Visit and Africa-Singapore Business Forum, and leverage South Africa's 2025 G20 Presidency.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: This year, we will host the Singapore-Africa Ministerial Exchange Visit and the Africa-Singapore Business Forum, to promote political and business engagements.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: We will also leverage South Africa's 2025 G20 Presidency to step up our engagement of African countries through bilateral exchanges, capacity building and cooperation in FinTech and digitalisation.

sections.label: India Comprehensive Strategic Partnership
sections.summary: During Prime Minister Narendra Modi's visit last September, relations were upgraded to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership with new cooperation areas.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: During Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s visit to Singapore last September, we agreed to upgrade relations to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership, which will include the expansion of cooperation into new and forward-looking areas, such as semiconductor ecosystems, next-generation industrial parks, and skilling.

sections.label: Johor Bilateral Initiatives
sections.summary: Besides the JS-SEZ and RTS Link, Singapore is working on renewable energy cooperation and more resilient supply chains.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: In addition to the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ) and the Johor Bahru-Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link, Singapore is working on other bilateral initiatives, including renewable energy cooperation as well as ways to make our supply chains more resilient, given our deep interdependencies.

sections.label: Low-Carbon Electricity Imports
sections.summary: The EMA granted conditional approval to five projects to import 3.4 gigawatts of low-carbon electricity from Indonesia within five years.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: For instance, the Energy Market Authority (EMA) has granted conditional approval to five projects to import a total of 3.4 gigawatts of low-carbon electricity from Indonesia within the next five years.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: This would constitute our largest-ever cross-border electricity contract while catalysing Indonesia’s renewable energy and adjacent industries.

sections.label: ASEAN trade and digital agreements
sections.summary: Singapore is reducing trade and investment barriers within ASEAN and with external partners, upgrading ATIGA and concluding DEFA this year.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: We are reducing barriers to trade and investment both within ASEAN and with our external partners.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: We will upgrade the ASEAN Trade in Goods Agreement (ATIGA), as well as substantially conclude the ASEAN Digital Economy Framework Agreement (DEFA) this year.

sections.label: Singapore position on Myanmar arms
sections.summary: Singapore has taken a principled position in line with the UN General Assembly resolution calling on member states to prevent arms flows into Myanmar.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: Singapore has taken a principled position, in line with the UN General Assembly resolution, which called on UN member states to prevent the flow of arms into Myanmar.

sections.label: Ambassador Rena Lee UN nomination
sections.summary: Ambassador Rena Lee is well-qualified with extensive international experience, and is Singapore's first nominee for this position since joining the UN.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Ambassador Rena Lee is well-qualified, with extensive experience in a wide range of international domains.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: This is the first time Singapore has nominated someone for this position since we joined the UN.

sections.label: SCP training over 33 years
sections.summary: Over 33 years, SCP trained more than 155,000 officials from over 180 countries, territories and organisations, including over 50,000 in Singapore Cooperation Centres.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Over the past 33 years, SCP has trained more than 155,000 officials from more than 180 countries, territories and intergovernmental organisations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Over 50,000 officials were trained in our Singapore Cooperation Centres in Cambodia, Laos, Vietnam and Myanmar.

sections.label: MFA consular cases and e-registrants
sections.summary: Last year MFA handled over 4,000 consular cases, facilitated over 2,000 Documents of Identity, and saw a 54% increase in e-registrants.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Last year, MFA handled more than 4,000 consular cases and facilitated more than 2,000 Documents of Identity for Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Last year, we saw a 54% increase in the number of e-registrants.

sections.label: Major powers and agreements
sections.summary: Some major powers have not signed UNCLOS or the Paris Agreement, making these agreements hard to enforce and implement without their participation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Because they will say, no, I have not.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: I mean, for instance, there are major powers that have not signed on to UNCLOS.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: There are major powers which are not signed on to the Paris Agreement.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: And it is very hard to make these agreements enforceable and implementable without the participation of major powers.

sections.label: US rebuilt vanquished countries
sections.summary: The passage states that after World War II the United States, a benevolent victor, rebuilt Japan, Germany and Europe through the Marshall Plan.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: The unique blessing after World War II was that there was a very benevolent victor in the United States of America, which rebuilt the countries it vanquished: Japan, Germany, Europe, through the Marshall Plan, which I had mentioned just now, because it constituted 40% of global GDP.

sections.label: ASEAN Myanmar envoy rotation reform
sections.summary: Commentators note annual ASEAN chair rotation means a new Myanmar special envoy each year, and suggest a permanent secretariat dedicated to Myanmar.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: It has been pointed out by commentators that one of the difficulties is that because of the annual rotation of country chair in ASEAN, a new special envoy is appointed each year and it seems that the work sort of starts all over again.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: It has been suggested that one of the reforms that could be considered is that ASEAN might set up a permanent secretariat that is dedicated to Myanmar, with staff that specialise in the issue and can provide more institutional memory and support to the special envoy.

sections.label: Changing envoys and strategic patience
sections.summary: The passage states envoys can be changed or made permanent, and that the speaker has urged strategic patience at ASEAN meetings.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: So, the problem is, we can change envoys; we can have special envoys; we can have permanent envoys.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: I have consistently urged at ASEAN meetings that we need strategic patience.

sections.label: Five-Point Consensus and no progress
sections.summary: The Five-Point Consensus arose from Senior Minister Lee's April 2021 Jakarta speech with all ASEAN countries represented, but the passage says there has been no progress.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Any ASEAN country, all ASEAN countries will be most happy to support them.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: That was the formula behind the Five-Point Consensus, if we look at the points in there.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: They arose out of a speech which Senior Minister Lee made at that special meeting that was convened in April 2021 in Jakarta where all the ASEAN countries were represented, including the military leader in Myanmar.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: But I am sorry to say, there has been no progress.

sections.label: Reviewing new African missions
sections.summary: The passage states missions in countries evolved from NRAs' work and that African countries and Africa as a region will continue to be reviewed for new Missions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: You will see the evolution of us setting up missions in countries from the work of some of our NRAs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: We will continue to review the African countries and the potential for Africa as a region for us to see if we will be able to set up new Missions in that area.

sections.label: Eviction from Malaysia over multiracial ideal
sections.summary: The passage states that sixty years ago Singapore was evicted from Malaysia for believing in a multiracial Singaporean Singapore, not an Indian, Malay or Chinese nation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Sixty years ago, for the sake of a belief in an ideal that we will be a multiracial society, a Singaporean Singapore, not based on being an Indian, Malay or Chinese nation, we were evicted from Malaysia.

sections.label: Trade volume and PSA
sections.summary: Singapore's trade volume is more than three times its GDP, a ratio no other political entity has.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: You look at PSA, airports, our trade volume more than three times our GDP.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: No other political entity has that ratio in the world.

sections.label: Pioneer leaders and changed rules
sections.summary: The speaker credits Pioneer leaders, disciplined Singaporeans and a kind global environment, and says the rules have changed.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: So, understand how blessed we have been by the Pioneer leaders and the hardworking and disciplined Singaporeans and the global environment which was very kind to us.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Now I am saying, the rules have changed.

sections.label: City state strengths and reserves
sections.summary: The speaker is excited by revolutions and opportunities, and is confident in a city state's fiscal reserves and Singapore's ministers not needing to ask for help.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: So, my point is, I am actually excited because I see a world in which there are revolutions with great opportunities.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: And I am confident that the strengths of a city state with fiscal reserves, and that a Prime Minister or a Foreign Minister of Singapore, at least in the next 10 years, does not have to go to any other capital or any other office with his hands asking for help.

sections.label: City as magnet for talent
sections.summary: A city must act as a magnet for ideas, talent and opportunity, and the speaker seeks leave to withdraw his cut.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: The thing about a city is that it must always act as a magnet for ideas, for talent, for opportunity.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: So, therefore, I still, I am very tempted to say the best is yet to be.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: Chairman, I seek leave to withdraw my cut.
